rules.rule: Every new code path or opt-in feature must be accompanied by a dedicated regression or coverage test that would fail if the feature were removed.
rules.reason: The /init files describe how to run tests and mention t.plan() accuracy, but never state that every new code path or opt-in feature requires a dedicated test that would fail if the feature were removed.

rules.rule: When a new hook, option, or API is added to the runtime, its TypeScript overload in types/*.d.ts must be updated in the same PR; omitting it causes excess-property or compile-time errors for TypeScript consumers.
rules.initQuote: Type definitions live under [`types/`](types/) and are re-exported via [`fastify.d.ts`](fastify.d.ts).
rules.reason: The init file locates the type definitions and mentions type tests, but never states that runtime additions must be accompanied by a types/*.d.ts update in the same PR.

rules.rule: New route-registration or framework failures must throw a named FST_ERR_* code instead of a plain Error so consumers can identify the failure programmatically.
rules.initQuote: All errors must be created with `@fastify/error` and registered in `lib/errors.js` with a `FST_ERR_*` code. Do not throw plain `Error` objects from framework internals.
rules.reason: The rules-agent file explicitly forbids plain Error objects from framework internals and requires FST_ERR_* codes, directly covering the rule.

rules.rule: Documentation must not overstate or contradict actual runtime behaviour; when a guard has known exceptions or bypasses, the prose must be scoped accurately and all parameters must be described.
rules.reason: None of the /init files mention accuracy requirements for documentation or the need to scope prose to actual runtime behaviour.

rules.rule: Each API option section in the reference docs must contain exactly one default-value entry; duplicate default declarations must be removed.
rules.reason: None of the /init files mention documentation formatting rules or prohibit duplicate default-value declarations.

rules.rule: Doc examples that delete symbol-keyed properties must use Object.getOwnPropertySymbols() or Reflect.ownKeys(); Object.keys() never returns symbol keys and silently skips the intended operation.
rules.reason: None of the /init files mention the limitation of Object.keys() with symbol keys or require the use of Object.getOwnPropertySymbols() in doc examples.
